pages: Outliers in labels (label noise) can skew the results of logistic regression modeling. One solution to reduce the impact of contamination on estimates is to use a robust version of logistic regression1. Robust Logistic Regression This model works by introducing the mixture of the two “sources” of labels, the model and the random (outlier) process. The robust probability curve is pulled toward 0.5 where the model is uncertain, making the fit more robust to the presence of outliers. 1. Kevin P. Murphy. Probabilistic Machine Learning: An Introduction, MIT, 2022.

import numpy as np from scipy.special import expit as sigmoid def robust_logistic_regression( X, y, epsilon=0.05, max_iter=30, tol=1e-6 ): """Robust Logistic Regression.""" n_features = X.shape[1] beta = np.zeros(n_features) q = 0.5 * np.ones_like(y, dtype=float) for _ in range(max_iter): z = X @ beta # Logit p = sigmoid(z) # Inverse logit # Assign probabilities to true label p_model = np.where(y = 1, p, 1 - p) # Calculate weights numerator = (1 - epsilon) * p_model denominator = numerator + epsilon * q w = numerator / denominator # Calculate weights and score W_diag = w * p * (1 - p) score = X.T @ (w * (y - p)) # Calculate weighted Fisher information fisher_info = X.T @ (W_diag[:, np.newaxis] * X) try: # Update step beta_new = np.linalg.inv(fisher_info) @ score except np.linalg.LinAlgError: beta_new = np.linalg.pinv(fisher_info) @ score beta += beta_new if np.linalg.norm(beta_new) < tol: # Convergence break return beta Below we provide a sketch implementation of mixture log likelihood with Fisher scoring with Python 🐍1: Robust Logistic Regression 1. Here we provide the Fisher Scoring algorithm example, which leverages Fisher information to estimate the coefficients, beta. Other alternatives to fitting are SGD (using only first-order gradients) and Bayesian logistic regression with pymc. Notebook with examples: https://lnkd.in/esHjSmZZ https://lnkd.in/esHjSmZZ
